fit: turmeric constituent in enzyme and cell studies
assessment: Curcumin is linked to turmeric and studied in protein kinase C pathways. Experimental kinase inhibition and other signaling are mechanistic endpoints. No ground-turmeric Parkinson pain comparison.
The review names coffee as a source of caffeic and chlorogenic acids. The sections summarize isolated compound effects outside fatigue. No separate effect from brewed coffee.

fit: sweet basil rosmarinic acid and kinase context
assessment: Rosmarinic acid in sweet basil is linked to isolated compound kinase experiments. No evaluation of dried basil intake, clinical fatigue or Parkinson disease.

fit: green tea constituent and kinase context
assessment: Reports isolated EGCG in PKC signaling experiments, including enzyme and cell-system outcomes. No green-tea infusion or Parkinson fatigue assessment.
Egg yolk is used as a homogenized substrate for lipid-peroxidation measurements. The intervention is a plant extract, without whole-egg consumption, a fall outcome or a person-level comparison.

fit: grape juice, polyphenols and modeled motor outcomes
assessment: The review links grape-derived exposures including mixed whole-grape and knotweed extract in a fly climbing study. The cited compounds, products and motor proxies differ from raw grape and human Parkinson rigidity.

fit: extract and distinct multiple sclerosis fatigue measures
assessment: Separate review passages discuss multiple sclerosis fatigue management and list green tea EGCG among candidate neuroprotectants. The candidate list supplies no EGCG-specific fatigue comparison.
The capsule summary points to Noorbala PMID 15707766, an existing stigma extract versus fluoxetine study. It does not add a placebo arm, a ground-spice comparison or an independent population.

fit: dietary carotenoid carrier and immune outcome
assessment: The review's immune table cites carotenoids dissolved in corn oil and an oil-only placebo. The cited study examined blood monocyte markers, with no depression endpoint or oil-free arm.

fit: same registration and separate published denominator
assessment: The Persian original reports 64 participants and lower acute labor-pain VAS at 60 minutes, with an inconclusive 30-minute contrast. It cites the same date-syrup registration as Taavoni. Later comparison counts and control data limit interpretation.

fit: same protocol honey arm and potentially shared controls
assessment: Honey versus water provides registration and cohort provenance, without a date comparison. Five control VAS means and SDs match the date-syrup report exactly, while one row differs.

fit: whole dates among offered foods, pooled pain outcome
assessment: At 6–7 cm dilation and in transition, pain was lower in the group permitted dates, juice and water compared with fasting. No preparation-specific or date-only comparison is reported. Possible overlap with a second report is unresolved.

fit: date fruit or orange juice and pooled labor progress
assessment: The offered-carbohydrate arm could choose dates with water or tea, or orange juice. The comparison reports labor progression and analgesic use. It does not provide an ingredient-specific measured pain result.
Both carotenoid and placebo capsules contain corn oil. The trial evaluates monocyte immune markers in healthy men. There is no contrast isolating the oil, refined grade or depression effect.

fit: isolated catechin and exercise energy use in multiple sclerosis
assessment: The crossover measured metabolism at rest and during cycling in multiple sclerosis. The source gives no dedicated fatigue severity result that transfers to the brewed-green-tea Parkinson claim.

fit: mixed grape and knotweed extract and model locomotion
assessment: The authors report improved fly climbing after a whole-grape and knotweed extract. The co-ingredient, modeled disease, outcome and preparation preclude a direct raw-grape rigidity estimate.
